h: Fairyland, the Dream Cave and the craft of Blue John
p: The story of Treak Cliff took an exciting turn in the 1920s, when miners digging for Blue John broke through into natural caverns that nobody had seen before. Those chambers are now some of the prettiest parts of the visit, with names like Fairyland and the Dream Cave that give you a hint of what to expect: delicate formations, flowstone and stalactites that seem to glow under the lights.

Back above ground, the museum and shop are worth more than a quick glance. Seeing how the raw stone is cut, shaped and polished into finished pieces really helps you appreciate the craft, and how much skill goes into turning a rough lump into something beautiful. If you're after a special souvenir, this is the place to pick one up straight from the source.

How long to allow? A visit here fits comfortably into a morning or an afternoon, leaving the rest of the day free for walking or exploring the village. If you've booked one of the hands-on Blue John experiences, add extra time for that.

Tips: wear proper footwear with a decent grip, take the climb to the entrance at your own pace and bring a layer for underground. Keep an eye on younger children on the steps, which can be slippery in places.

Walkers will love the location. From here, paths lead up towards Mam Tor and along the Great Ridge to Hollins Cross and beyond, with some of the best views in the Peak District. Head back down into Castleton afterwards for a well-earned pub lunch or a cream tea.
